In [[commutative algebra]], an '''analytically normal ring''' is a [[local ring]] whose [[completion (ring theory)|completion]] is a [[normal ring]]; in other words, an [[integral domain]] that is [[integral closure|integrally closed]] in its [[quotient field]].

[[Oscar Zariski|Zariski]]{{sfnp|Zariski|1950}} proved that if a local ring of an [[algebraic variety]] is normal, then it is analytically normal, which is in some sense a variation of [[Zariski's main theorem]]. [[Masayoshi Nagata|Nagata]]{{sfnp|Nagata|1958}}{{sfnp|Nagata|1962|loc=appendix A1, example 7}} gave an example of a normal [[Noetherian ring|Noetherian]] local ring that is [[analytically reducible]] and therefore not analytically normal.
